sprinkle salt: Before grilling the fish, my mother likes to sprinkle salt and a little pepper over both sides.
烤魚之前，我媽媽喜歡在魚的兩面撒鹽和一點胡椒。
sprinkled with humor: The principal's speech was sprinkled with humor, so even the sleepy students laughed and listened carefully.
校長的演講點綴著幽默，所以連想睡的學生都笑了並認真聆聽。
sprinkle water: On hot afternoons, the shop owner would sprinkle water on the sidewalk to keep the dust down.
炎熱的午後，店主會在人行道上灑水來壓住灰塵。
sprinkle sugar on: When the pancakes are ready, sprinkle sugar on top and serve them with fresh strawberries.
鬆餅做好後，在上面撒糖，再搭配新鮮草莓上桌。
spur growth: The government hopes that lower taxes will spur growth and create thousands of new jobs next year.
政府希望降低稅收能刺激成長，並在明年創造數千個新工作。
spur someone on: When I felt like giving up, the loud cheers of my classmates would spur me on to the finish line.
當我想放棄時，同學們響亮的加油聲會激勵我衝向終點線。
spur innovation: Many companies hold idea contests to spur innovation and encourage young workers to share creative plans.
許多公司舉辦點子競賽來激發創新，並鼓勵年輕員工分享有創意的計畫。
on the spur of the moment: We didn't plan the trip at all; we just drove to the beach on the spur of the moment.
我們完全沒有計畫這趟旅行；我們只是一時衝動就開車去了海邊。
spur demand: Big holiday discounts often spur demand for new phones, so stores hire extra workers in December.
大型節日折扣常常刺激新手機的需求，所以商店在十二月會多雇員工。
spy on someone: She felt uncomfortable when she realized her nosy neighbor used to spy on someone through the window every night.
當她發現好管閒事的鄰居每晚都透過窗戶監視某人時，她感到很不舒服。
spy a figure in the distance: Standing on the hill, the hikers could spy a figure in the distance waving a red flag at them.
站在山丘上，登山客們瞥見遠處人影正朝他們揮動一面紅旗。
spy an opportunity: Smart business owners quickly spy an opportunity when they notice something that customers really need.
聰明的老闆一注意到顧客真正需要的東西，就會很快發現機會。
spy out the land: Before moving the whole army forward, the general sent two soldiers ahead to spy out the land.
在讓整支軍隊前進之前，將軍先派兩名士兵到前方探路。
squander money: If you squander money on snacks and games every day, you will never save enough for the trip.
如果你每天把錢揮霍在零食和遊戲上，你永遠存不夠旅行的錢。
squander an opportunity: Don't squander an opportunity like this; scholarships to study abroad are offered to only three students a year.
別浪費這樣的機會；出國留學的獎學金每年只提供給三名學生。
squander one's talent: His coach warned him not to squander his talent by skipping practice and staying up late every night.
他的教練警告他，不要因為翹掉練習又每晚熬夜而糟蹋自己的才華。
squander a lead: Our team managed to squander a lead of twenty points in the last quarter and lost the final game.
我們隊在最後一節竟把二十分的領先優勢揮霍掉，輸掉了決賽。
squash a rumor: The school released the facts on its website to squash a rumor that classes would be canceled.
學校在網站上公布事實，以粉碎課程將被取消的謠言。
squash a rebellion: The king sent thousands of soldiers to squash a rebellion that had started in the northern villages.
國王派出數千名士兵去鎮壓在北方村莊爆發的叛亂。
squash hopes: The heavy rain seemed to squash hopes of holding the outdoor concert, so the fans went home sadly.
大雨似乎打碎了舉辦戶外演唱會的希望，所以歌迷們難過地回家了。
squash into the car: Six of us had to squash into the car, sitting shoulder to shoulder for the whole two-hour ride.
我們六個人只好擠進車裡，整整兩小時的車程都肩並肩地坐著。
squash the idea: Our manager decided to squash the idea of a weekend picnic because the budget was too small.
我們經理決定否決週末野餐的想法，因為預算太少了。
squeeze profits: Rising rent and higher prices for coffee beans continue to squeeze profits at small cafés in the city.
上漲的租金和更貴的咖啡豆持續壓縮市區小咖啡館的利潤。
squeeze in a meeting: The doctor is very busy today, but she will try to squeeze in a meeting with you after lunch.
醫生今天很忙，但她會試著在午餐後擠出時間跟你開會。
squeeze money out of: The dishonest salesman tried to squeeze money out of old people by selling them useless health products.
那個不誠實的推銷員試圖向老人推銷沒用的保健品，以榨取他們的錢財。
feel the squeeze: When food and gas prices go up, many families begin to feel the squeeze at the end of each month.
當食物和油價上漲時，許多家庭在每個月底開始感到經濟壓力。
squeeze through: The cat was small enough to squeeze through the narrow gap in the fence and escape into the garden.
那隻貓夠小，可以從籬笆的窄縫擠過去，逃進花園裡。
squeeze the budget: The new rules squeeze the budget so tightly that the club can no longer pay for the year-end party.
新規定把預算壓縮得非常緊，社團再也付不起年終派對的費用了。
